newsitem.title: FRANCE: Zimbabwe's Mugabe to push truce with Zaire rebels.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe's Mugabe to push truce with Zaire rebels.

text.p: Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe said on Friday he would try to persuade Tutsi-led rebels fighting the Zairean government to accept a U.N. plan to end the crisis in the African nation.

The plan, which calls for a ceasefire, the withdrawal of all foreign troops and the protection of refugees, has been accepted by Kinshasa, but the rebels link a truce to talks on an end to the 31-year rule of President Mobutu Sese Seko.

"On our part, we shall undertake to talk to the other side, to the rebels and others to find out whether they too are prepared to go along," Mugabe told reporters after meeting France's President Jacques Chirac on a visit to Paris.
"We did agree that it was necessary for us both to support as an urgent matter the peace plan...and that all parties involved should agree to the plan," Mugabe added.

Mugabe said he and Chirac had agreed that "none other than the people of Africa" should make up a U.N.-proposed international force to open humanitarian corridors "and the others should come behind and support our efforts."
Mugabe said Chirac had accepted his invitation to visit Zimbabwe but did not say when the visit would take place.
Tutsi-led rebels who took up arms against Mobutu's government in October and seized towns and territory in the east have named Kisangani as their next target.
Mobutu is resting up from prostate surgery in his villa on the French Riviera.
